task.description: Design the corrected resolveTenantSlug/1 contract handling both ordinary tenants and the pinned default tenant.

result.note: Root fix: before applying the existing realm.startsWith('bpm-') ? realm.slice(4) : realm rule, check for the literal reserved realm bpm-default and return it verbatim (no stripping); all other branches (tenant_id-claim priority, try/catch URL parsing, non-bpm-prefixed fallback) unchanged. Hardcode chosen over a pattern rule: verified tenant.ex:73 really does define @default_tenant_slug bpm-default as a hardcoded module attribute, and validate_default_tenant_pinning/1 (lines 147-159) enforces idp_realm_id == bpm-default exactly for that one tenant -- no shape-based rule can distinguish realm bpm-default -> slug bpm-default from realm bpm-acme1 -> slug acme1 purely from string structure (both are bpm- + suffix), the distinguishing fact isn't recoverable from the string itself, so an exact-literal check mirroring tenant.ex's own hardcoded-constant style is correct and non-over-generalizing. Frontend-only hardcode recommended over a backend-signaled approach, per ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis that minting a tenant_id JWT claim is a multi-file Keycloak-provisioning lift repeating an already-documented unresolved mapper-drift gap (contract-gaps.md:51-70). Known tradeoff explicitly flagged, not silently ignored: the literal bpm-default in tokenUtils.ts must stay in sync with tenant.ex's @default_tenant_slug, a future change to the pinned value would silently drift -- left for REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGNER to decide if a follow-up (shared constant, cross-reference comment) is warranted. Open questions listed, not resolved: whether a tenant literally slugged 'default' colliding with the ordinary-convention realm bpm-default is currently permitted by REQ-019's validations; a code comment cross-referencing tenant.ex should be added at the hardcoded check site. Test cases specified for web/src/auth/__tests__/tokenUtils.test.ts (currently doesn't test resolveTenantSlug at all): (1) realm bpm-default -> slug bpm-default (the regression test), (2) realm bpm-acme1 -> slug acme1 (general-case regression guard), (3) tenant_id claim still takes priority over realm parsing, (4) no iss/tenant_id -> null. Includes an acceptance-criteria-to-design-element mapping table (SS8).
